title: Career roadmap · Regulatory Counsel
summary: Build from technology, AI and data-protection law into regulatory interpretation, compliance strategy, technology governance and senior regulatory advisory work.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap starts in 2026 and follows the 2026–2046 horizons. Because the student is already pursuing a Ph.D., the early years focus on producing specialised legal research, regulatory-analysis work and practical compliance outputs that can support counsel-level roles.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Technology-law researcher, privacy researcher, regulatory analyst, AI-governance researcher or legal-policy fellow.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Specialise in AI regulation, data protection, cybersecurity regulation, platform governance, financial technology or emerging-technology regulation.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Move into senior regulatory counsel, regulatory strategy, compliance leadership and complex technology-governance advisory work.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Lead regulatory strategy for emerging technologies while tracking AI, data, cybersecurity, digital competition and cross-border regulatory change.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Regulatory counsel should remain capable of interpreting new rules before they become settled practice. Build expertise across law, technology architecture, risk management, regulatory economics and international frameworks rather than specialising in one statute alone.

blocks.label: Career progression
blocks.text: Ph.D. Researcher → Technology/Privacy Law Researcher → Regulatory Analyst → Regulatory Counsel → Senior Regulatory Counsel → Regulatory Strategy Lead → Head of Regulatory Affairs → Chief Regulatory/Policy Counsel

blocks.label: Typical years
blocks.text:
2026–2030 → research/regulatory analyst roles
2030–2035 → specialist counsel
2035–2040 → senior counsel/regulatory strategy
2040–2046 → regulatory leadership
Ph.D./research routes

Regulatory counsel will need to understand not only statutes and regulatory orders but also how AI systems, data architectures, cybersecurity controls and digital platforms actually operate. Maintain legal scholarship while developing enough technical literacy to interrogate risk assessments, governance frameworks and regulatory-impact claims.
